| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| S240-001 | 🟠 HIGH | crates/cli/src/statusline.rs | 338-390 | A separate unregistered nested Copilot can display its registered parent's seat identity | 9/10 |

S240-001: With no tmux pane, a separately launched Copilot B can inherit registered Copilot A's PIJ_SESSION_ID. The paneless whoami branch resolves A, then runs_under accepts any matching ancestor PID+start. For the ordinary descendant chain A -> B -> wrapper/statusline, the walk reaches A and prints A's seat name (and its status), despite the status line belonging to B. It checks no intermediate harness/session boundary, so matching the recorded start does not distinguish wrappers under A from another Copilot host under A. This is accidental misattribution within F198's stated contract, not a same-user adversarial isolation requirement or a newly discovered permission-escalation exploit.

Sources: crates/cli/src/main.rs:2595-2614; crates/cli/src/statusline.rs:338-390. The new regression's chain is 500 -> 400 -> 300, while its inherited foreign identity uses PID 4242, outside the chain (crates/cli/src/statusline_tests.rs:665-768). It therefore does not pin this case. This finding is a source-derived counterexample, not a live reproduction of the candidate binary. Preserve shell-wrapper support, but distinguish a second Copilot host/session before accepting a more distant registered ancestor; extend the existing regression with that concrete chain.

Other reviewed behavior:
- Direct-parent and shell-wrapper ancestry is supported: the managed script execs the CLI (harness/scripts/copilot-statusline-pij.sh:11-12). The walk inspects 64 nodes, self plus at most 63 ancestors, and matches PID and start (statusline.rs:373-390). A deeper match is withheld. macOS parent/start reads use PID-checked ProcBSDShortInfo/ProcBSDInfo; Linux reads /proc (crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:158-168,258-271,345-383). macOS was read by eye, not compiled or executed here.
- Pane lookup discards inherited session identity; remote, unbound, recycled and unrelated processes fail the new guard. Refusals emit fixed text rather than the named seat or remote response prose (main.rs:2492-2516,2568-2614; statusline.rs:304-390). This does not claim blanket sanitization of unrelated pre-existing statusline fields. The display guard is a brake: removing it can expose more names; it does not retire or kill seats.
- F195 selects native Copilot delivery, uses monotonic elapsed lease time and saturating numeric formatting, and reevaluates renewal rather than latching a lapse. Local roster projection excludes tombstones. New state/list text consists of fixed prose, numeric age and closed-vocabulary liveness, not arbitrary external text. Sources: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:530-596; crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:3645-3681,3818-3829,4111-4120; crates/core/src/cold_wake.rs:315-322. State's separate lease reads can race; absent age omits the since clause. Never-renewed and recovered-card field removal lack dedicated new assertions; those proof gaps alone are not gates under C34.
- No additional changed-code secret, supply-chain, shell/path-injection or external-text-rendering vulnerability was identified. C33 is applied at the user-account boundary.

Cost:
- Copilot statusline: configured every 10 seconds per session, approximately 0.1 renders/s/session. The ownership addition launches zero child processes, adds zero daemon requests, and uses the existing whoami answer plus bounded in-process parent/start reads (main.rs:2568-2614; statusline.rs:373-390). Approximately 50 sessions means approximately 5 renders/s. This is zero NEW launches, not zero total launches: the existing CLI invocation and exceptional git fallback remain (statusline.rs:596-601,687-704).
- State adds one in-memory lease lookup per call. List adds one in-memory read over the listed seats, O(seats) per call. No renew-loop, poll or timer change.
- crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs is unchanged. Its guards cover harness/daemon launch sites, but explicitly exclude CLI processes; the added CLI ownership path was inspected directly (spawn_sites.rs:1-24,202-242,285-353).
- Baseline, 2026-11-18 03:15:28Z to 03:15:48Z: same daemon PID 46800; spawn total 793 -> 793, all by_op counters unchanged, 0 daemon launches/s over 20 seconds. just spawn-rate --seconds 20 reported 108.3 machine-wide launches/s, sampled 106.1/s, no observed daemon children and 0 observed statusline runs/s.
